title: Stopping a turn pauses the session's queue, so mailbox recovery wakes are held ("heldBehindPausedQueue") until someone resumes the queue
outcome: A queue held only by a due automatic Engram retry is shown as that retry (its cause and next due time) in the mailbox disposition, the session API and the UI, never as a bare pause, so nobody resumes a self-recovering session by hand. Criteria proposed by Termal::Opus3 (TermAl mailbox 03723eab #3338) and concurred verbatim by Termal::Fable2 in note a0896b2d.
acceptance: While an automatic Engram retry owns a session's head (admission, begin-preparation, abort or bind retry with a due time), the mailbox wake disposition is a distinct value, e.g. "waitingForAutomaticRetry", never heldBehindPausedQueue. The session API states the hold's cause and next due time. Fail-first tests drive each of the three real producers seen today (begin_preparation_pending, control_unavailable at the named-root guard, dispatch_budget_exhausted) through the real dispatch path, then the due tick delivers the wake once with no Resume.

Stop, an operator pause, a retained explicit hold (no due retry), Cancel, retry exhaustion and changed authority keep heldBehindPausedQueue and queuePaused exactly as today. The latch's own semantics are unchanged. Tests cover each negative.
The UI shows the same cause and retry time instead of a bare "paused". The census and coordinator tooling can tell the two apart from the API alone.
The stale TRAIN-5 package (a694b626) is formally superseded on the item, not carried.
